sara-nguyen: FYI, hit a weird failure during FP8 bake on dedicated pool (rtx-a6000, CUDA 12.2 + driver 535). TRT-LLM path keeps falling back and we see 3x latency + 4-6% quality delta compared to the host vLLM path. logs attached inline. :grimacing:

ben: can you paste a repro / minimal log? is it runtime segfault or kernel fallback?

sara-nguyen: no segfault, just repeated kernel fallthroughs and `TRTLLM_FALLBACK=1` kicks in. sample log: ```
[2026-03-18T16:22:10Z] trtllm: kernel_select: unsupported kernel for op_attention_ft8 -> fallthrough
[2026-03-18T16:22:10Z] trtllm: using fallback runtime (vllm-compatible) for layer 9
[2026-03-18T16:22:10Z] runtime: latency 120ms -> fallback path 370ms
```

akshay: hmm. similar to a mismatch I saw when cuBLAS/driver combo changed. Which container base and tensorrt-llm version?

sara-nguyen: container: rdx-infer:cuda12.2-2026-03 (ubuntu22.04), trt-llm 1.4.2, vllm 0.9.7, awq/gptq outputs used in quant build.

ben: two possibilities: (1) quant format uses fused attention that TRTLLM doesn't support for this arch+version, (2) driver/cuDNN ABI mismatch causing kernel selector to be conservative. Have you tried forcing the non-fused kernels?

sara-nguyen: quick test: set `TRTLLM_DISABLE_FUSED=1` and restarted. latency dropped compared to full fallback, but accuracy took a small hit vs original FP8 run (maybe due to different kernel numerics).

ops-jen: CI alert showed increased error rate on canary, rolling back to INT8 GPTQ variant reduced errors. We should gate FP8 on a driver compatibility matrix. :warning:

ci-bot: automated: failed bake: fp8-q8-runner on pool-dedicated-rtx-a6000 (job 8291) -> marked flaky.

akshay: actionable items: 1) repro with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` + `TRTLLM_DISABLE_FUSED=1` to isolate kernel selection vs async launch issues. 2) try driver 540 on staging (we saw kernel selector improvements there). 3) run comparison eval set (1k prompts) to quantify accuracy delta for FP8 vs INT8+GPTQ/AWQ.

sara-nguyen: putting commands here: ```bash
# repro env
export CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1
export TRTLLM_DISABLE_FUSED=1
python -m rdx.infer.run --model /mnt/models/ensemble-13b-fp8 --quant-format awq --engine trtllm --batch 8 --seq 1024
```

ben: also try `LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so` if you suspect loader mismatches in the container. had one case where container used mismatched libcuda at runtime.

sara-nguyen: good call — will try both. i ran a quick eval w/ the `20k-regress` prompt set: FP8 (baseline) -> 86.3% pass; fallback-trt->vllm -> 81.1%; INT8-GPTQ -> 85.6%. so fallback is the problem, not FP8 itself.

akshay: that pattern screams selective kernel fallback on a few attention variants. If Triton/Triton-LLM kernel registry lacks the fused variant for FP8, it falls back mid-sequence and cache gets mismatched leading to quality deltas.

ops-jen: pragmatic mitigation: 1) pin to INT8-GPTQ on the dedicated pool while we validate driver 540 on staging, 2) add runtime feature-detection at startup to disable FP8 engine when incompatible (health-check).

sara-nguyen: agreed. i'll open a short PR to add a startup probe that tests fused attention kernels and flips `engine=trtllm` -> `engine=vllm` or `engine=int8` based on result. will include logs for the 1k eval.

ben: add a trace hook so we can see layer-level fallback counts in prod telemetry (per-request) — need to alert when fallback rate > 2%.

ci-bot: note: rollback workflow triggered for job 8291 at 2026-03-18T17:03:05Z.

sara-nguyen: timeline: try driver 540 tomorrow on staging, run 1k eval, and if good we schedule a canary deploy. if not, stick to INT8-GPTQ for prod-only pools. I'll post results here. :thumbsup:
